coverage: Read input.json in full: the assignment-2 prompt, the prior assignment-1 prompt, and all 24 criteria (21 required, 3 penalties; 73 positive points), with sources and justifications. Read the pinned upstream instruction.md (shared role prompt with an 8,750-word limit for a response brief; the agent may read its prior response1.md; the verifier reads only response2.md). The judge sees only each criterion's text. The six assignment-2 attachments are identical to the assignment-1 copies apart from their source lines, and were read as described in the assignment-1 report (motion and affidavits, complaint, Bradbury and Guerine in full; Langenhorst pp. 7-13 of the majority analysis; report pp. 19-22 and 163). Verified on CourtListener: Langenhorst ('exceptional circumstances'; no affidavits of inconvenience; defendants cannot assert that the plaintiff's forum is inconvenient to the plaintiff), Guerine (congestion 'relatively insignificant'), and Bradbury. Criteria 1-10, 13-17 and 19-24 were checked with no defect found. Penalties 23 and 24 correctly target misallocating the burden and claiming no deference (Langenhorst: deference is less, not none). Not flagged: criteria 19 and 20 cite report p. 21, but the civil-category figures (96.3% for the 18th Circuit, 97.9% for Cook) are on p. 22; the judge does not see the source field, so grading is unaffected. Criteria 1-5 describe the physicians as treating Baby Davis 'at Cook County Hospital' while the assignment-1 email names Lurie Children's Hospital in Cook County; the email also calls them 'Cook County Hospital Doctors', so a judge is unlikely to misgrade. No solver output was examined.

findings.title: Penalizes stating the 60.5% figure that the response brief must rebut
findings.explanation: Penalty misfire: the defendants' congestion argument rests 'principally' on Cook County's 60.5% all-case clearance rate. A response brief must answer it, and criteria 19 and 20 reward the answer: the civil-category rates of 96.3% (DuPage) and 97.9% (Cook). The persuasive way to make that point is to name the defendants' figure and show it measures all case types. The prompt also asks the response to 'include all ... information you referenced from Assignment #1', which for a good assignment-1 memo includes the 60.5% rebuttal. The judge sees only 'States in Assignment #2 that the 2023 Illinois Annual Report Statistics report a 60.5% clearance rate in Cook County, Illinois.' A brief that writes 'Defendants cite a 60.5% clearance rate, but that figure covers all case types' literally states it. Grading effect: -30 against 73 positive points (41% of the assignment), applied to a correct rebuttal of the defendants' main congestion argument.

authorities.citation: Langenhorst v. Norfolk Southern Ry. Co., 219 Ill. 2d 430, 848 N.E.2d 927 (2006)
authorities.proposition: Quoting Guerine: court congestion is a relatively insignificant factor, especially where the record does not show the other forum would resolve the case more quickly.

findings.suggested_fix: Penalize only a response that relies on or concedes the 60.5% all-case clearance rate as the measure of Cook County's congestion; do not penalize one that cites it to show it is the wrong comparison.

findings.title: Requires a sworn statement from the plaintiff that DuPage is inconvenient, with no record basis
findings.explanation: Criteria 11 and 12 (10 of 73 points) require the brief to rely on Sara Davis's affidavit stating that DuPage County would be inconvenient for her, 'as required under Langenhorst'. The record says only that she lives in Kane County; nothing says DuPage is inconvenient for her. The cited Langenhorst passage faults the defendants for filing no affidavits that the plaintiff's forum was inconvenient to witnesses; it does not require a plaintiff's affidavit, and defendants 'cannot assert that the plaintiff's chosen forum is inconvenient to the plaintiff'. A careful drafter may decline to put a sworn statement of inconvenience in the client's mouth without facts, and rely instead on the five physicians, who the record says find DuPage inconvenient (rewarded by criteria 1-10). Sequential dependency: the prompt asks for the affidavits 'you referenced from Assignment #1'. If the assignment-1 memo, permissibly, did not recommend a Sara Davis inconvenience affidavit, the prompt does not call for one here, yet criteria 11 and 12 still require it.

evidence.quote: Identifies in Assignment #2 that the affidavit by the Plaintiff, Sara Davis, indicates that DuPage County would be an inconvenient forum for her to litigate this case as required under Langenhorst v. Norfolk S. Ry. Co. 219 Ill. 2d 430 (Ill. 2006).
By way of background, our client, Sara Davis, resides in Kane County, Illinois.
Please include all affidavits and information you referenced from Assignment #1.

evidence.source: attachments/assignment-2/Langenhorst v. Norfolk Southern.pdf.md, PDF page 10
evidence.quote: In this case, no affidavits have been filed stating that St. Clair County would be an inconvenient forum for any of the witnesses.

authorities.citation: Langenhorst v. Norfolk Southern Ry. Co., 219 Ill. 2d 430, 848 N.E.2d 927 (2006)
authorities.proposition: Defendants, who bear the burden, filed no affidavits that the plaintiff's chosen forum was inconvenient for any witness; defendants cannot assert that the plaintiff's chosen forum is inconvenient to the plaintiff.

findings.suggested_fix: Make criteria 11 and 12 conditional on the assignment-1 recommendation, or give a factual basis for Sara Davis's inconvenience in the prompt; otherwise reward a residence affidavit or reliance on the physicians' affidavits.
